entries.blocked_by: ernie_mhc_pre_rms / ernie_mhc_head have no libr4d row in any weight format (4-1 inventory, story dev-*): the f32 matrix is read by the host libref op until a device row is written
entries.justification: The mHC mixing matrices feed a 20-iteration Sinkhorn and the residual stream mixing of every layer; an error here is multiplied through all 43 layers. Radiance stores the flagship model's mixing matrices as e4m3 rows or bf16 under its own fused read; ERNIE's ernie_mhc_pre_rms reads them f32 and has no device row in any format, and they are 0.26 GiB (0.2% of the model), so they stay f32 (rule: cast dtype=f32, the transpose the plugin already does). bf16 is the fallback once a kernel exists and the Sinkhorn sensitivity is measured.

entries.justification: The routed gate experts are 86% of the checkpoint (258 of 268.6 GiB), so they take the narrowest grid that keeps the model: IQR-V4's computed 16-bit trellis at four bits under one f32 scale a row (moe_gemm_iqr reads exactly this at i8a8h: N%16, K%128, 512 experts). Radiance's own four-bit candidate puts the trellis on its 512 routed experts and the Qwen3.8 V4 recipes on every FFN; IQR-V4 beats block FP8 at 55% of its size on the 27B. Expert GEMMs are the bandwidth term of decode, so the bytes are what pays.
entries.recipe_rule: blk.*.ffn_gate_exps.*.weight         gptq codes=u4 tcq=16 tcq_code=mad tcq_rows=512 block=1x* scale=f32 transform=fwht128 tcq_gain=1.12 damp=0.01 calib=$CALIB tcq_order=1

The two routers decide which 10 of 512 experts run and Baidu's gate computes its matmul and logits in f32 (moe-forward.md: a bf16 logit moves the output by more than 1e-3). Radiance keeps the router bf16 for the flagship MoE and for every MoE it serves. There is no quantised f32-arithmetic router row (gemm_nt_f32 has a bf16-weight row only), so IQ8R would need a new kernel; the bytes at stake are 0.34 GiB. The measured IQ8R top-10 agreement is in iqr-v4-layers.json (block kind router) as the evidence for that later lever.

entries.band_gap: no accepting row for M in ['2048']: gemm_iq8r_tiled: N multiple of 128 (given 576); gemm_iq8r_nt_m16: M <= 64 (given 2048)
entries.band_fallback: pad the weight's N to the next multiple of 128 at convert (576 -> 640: 64 zero rows, +11% of this matrix, +1.8 MiB over its 7 layers at int8, not in the memory plan) so the tiled prefill rows apply, or add an N%64 tile to libr4d; the rows gemm_iq8r_nt_m16 already serve the other bands

Radiance serves attention projections as int8 W8A8 for the flagship MoE and as rotated int8 (or u5 trellis for attn_output) in the Qwen IQR-V4 recipes; a 4-bit grid here buys 2.5 GiB and costs error in every token. IQ8R (gemm_iq8r_*, K a multiple of 256) it is.
entries.recipe_rule: blk.*.attn_output.weight             rtn codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search

entries.justification: The fp8 block-scale plane belongs to the SOURCE format only: the converter reads it to dequantise the weight and the serving container carries its own scales (IQR-V4: one f32 a row; IQ8R: u8 per 256 of K under a bf16 row scale). Nothing of it is served.

entries.blocked_by: ernie_mhc_pre_rms / ernie_mhc_head have no libr4d row in any weight format (4-1 inventory, story dev-*): the f32 matrix is read by the host libref op until a device row is written
entries.justification: The mHC mixing matrices feed a 20-iteration Sinkhorn and the residual stream mixing of every layer; an error here is multiplied through all 43 layers. Radiance stores the flagship model's mixing matrices as e4m3 rows or bf16 under its own fused read; ERNIE's ernie_mhc_pre_rms reads them f32 and has no device row in any format, and they are 0.26 GiB (0.2% of the model), so they stay f32 (rule: cast dtype=f32, the transpose the plugin already does). bf16 is the fallback once a kernel exists and the Sinkhorn sensitivity is measured.

The output head is 1.5 GiB bf16 and decode reads all of it every token; int8 rows with a bf16 scale a (row, 128) (logits_gemm_i8, n_embd % 128) is what every IQ8R recipe of this tree does, GPTQ'd against the head's input Hessian when one exists. The head's measured top-1 and KL against the bf16 head are in iqr-v4-layers.json. The vocabulary-weighted IQR head (logits_gemm_vocab_iqr) is the later size lever.
entries.recipe_rule: output.weight                        rtn codes=i8 group=128 scale=bf16 clamp=sym rule=search
